items.q: Fill up: Whole-kidney GFR equals single nephron GFR multiplied by the ______ of nephrons.
items.exp: GFR = single nephron GFR × number of nephrons. (Book p737)

items.q: Which sequence matches the book's hyperfiltration-injury note?
opts: ↓ nephron number → ↑ snGFR to maintain GFR → beyond compensation intraglomerular HTN → proteinuria → interstitial fibrosis → ↓ GFR
items.exp: Even if number ↓, snGFR ↑ to maintain GFR (hyperfiltration injury); beyond the point of compensation: intraglomerular HTN → proteinuria → interstitial fibrosis → ↓ GFR. (Book p737)

items.q: Fill up: Clearance equals urine concentration × urine volume (V) divided by the ______ concentration.
items.exp: Clearance = (urine concentration × volume of urine in ml/min (V)) / plasma concentration. (Book p737)

items.q: Endogenous creatinine clearance is written as:
items.exp: Endogenous Cr clearance = U_cr × V / P_cr. (Book p737)

items.q: Match each cystatin C fact with its descriptor — 1) Size 2) Biochemical class 3) Production … A) Constant rate by all nucleated cells B) 13 kDa molecule protein C) Cysteine protease inhibitor
items.exp: Cystatin C: 13 kDa molecule protein; cysteine protease inhibitor; produced at constant rate by all nucleated cells. (Book p737)

items.q: All of the following describe cystatin C handling EXCEPT:
opts: It is reabsorbed by the PCT
It is produced at a constant rate
It is secreted by the PCT
It is filtered but not secreted
items.exp: Cystatin C: filtered but not secreted; reabsorbed by PCT; constant production — it is never secreted. (Book p737)

items.q: Cystatin C is not affected by all of the following EXCEPT:
items.exp: Advantages: not affected by race, diet, muscle mass or drugs; inflammation (with steroids and smoking) elevates it non-specifically. (Book p737)

items.q: Fill up: Because of its non-specific elevations, cystatin C cannot replace ______.
Cystatin C is non-specifically elevated in inflammation, smokers and patients:
items.exp: Non specifically elevated in: inflammation, taking steroids, smokers. (Book p737)
